payload.body: task 2 (launch bump recompiles): approach — lift the stamped compile in `launch` into a `compileFor(n)` closure plus a `sizeFromCompile` helper; hand `pushPlan` the first N's compile and `recompile`, and have it recompile once per bumped N (after the purge, before the next attempt's hub filing), returning the compile the winning N was filed under. `launch` then reads width/cpu/memory off that returned compile for the `new` verb. The un-bumped path still makes exactly one stamped compile, before `new`. Capacity (`billing plan --json`) stays checked once on the first compile's size before any mutation: the widest wave does not depend on --stamp, so the recompiled size is the checked one.

payload.author: exam:1@run-128
payload.body:
examiner (task 1): writing `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs` as a `_engine_helpers.mjs` rig sim, four scenarios:

- S1 — one task with two Proof `Run:` lines (the second red on pass 0, green after the repair round) plus one Global Constraints `Check:`, and a `t1_test.sh` exam red at BASE / green on the patch. That single run records `impl:T1`, `exam:T1` and `fix:T1:0` prompts, which is legs (a) first half [M1], (b) [M2] and (c) [M3] in one place — and it is why leg (b)'s "the same `PROOFS:` block" can be asserted as string equality between the impl and fix prompts of the SAME task rather than across two runs.
- S2 — a task with no `Run:`, a run with no `Check:`, and the task still carrying its own `testCmd`: leg (a) second half. At BASE that prompt carries `TEST COMMAND: bash check.sh`, so the red is sharp.
- S3 — the implementer writes the rig's `BROKEN` marker, so the folded tree's `bash check.sh` is red once and a `reconcile:wave1:1` worker is dispatched; the stub removes the marker and reports FIXED so the wave still adopts. Leg (e) [M5].
- S4/S5 — the two greps as a static source read (leg (d) [M4]) and the two survivor sims' presence + `ALL TESTS PASSED` sentinel (leg (f) [M6]).

Two readings I am recording because a later session would otherwise have to re-derive them:

1. Block order. M1 says 'one line per Proof `Run:` ... and one line per ... `Check:` ... in plan order', and the Produces interface spells the block `\nPROOFS:\n- Run: <cmd>\n- Check: <cmd>`. I read that as all `- Run: ` lines in `task.proofRuns` order first, then all `- Check: ` lines in `constraintChecks` order — not interleaved — and the exam pins the exact substring.
2. The examiner's prompt. M3's 'unchanged from BASE' is asserted as: exactly one line beginning `TEST COMMAND:`, and it is exactly `TEST COMMAND: <the exam command>`. I deliberately do NOT assert the examiner has no `PROOFS:` block — nothing in the task asks for one, and pinning its absence would grade a choice the Machine clauses never make.

payload.author: exam:2@run-128
payload.body: Examiner: writing fleet/tests/test_launch_bump.mjs. Approach: the size sim's scaffolding, copied (its own header sets that convention) — a real target repo from _lobby_helpers with a bare origin, a recording exec, and a fake kata hub that stamps each call with the exec-call index so hub/exec ordering is readable. The bump is made real rather than faked: the rule that refuses the first push of ultra/plan-run-1 first pushes base:refs/heads/ultra/plan-run-1 onto the bare origin, so the launcher's own re-read of highestRunOnTarget sees 1 taken and bumps to 2 on its own. The compiler stub answers a stamp-dependent payload: run-1 -> waves 2/10/1 with sheets under tests/exams/run_1/, run-2 -> waves 2/4/1 with sheets under tests/exams/run_2/. Two payloads is how M3's 'the size the new verb carries is computed from the recompiled payload' becomes falsifiable at all — widest 10 is 6/8GB under the 6/8GB caps, widest 4 is 4/6GB, so a launch that sized off the first compile is red. Legs: (a) two stamped compiles run-1 then run-2, the second ordered after the refused push and before the second createProject, the project-2 sheets deep-equal to the run-2 payload's and no run_1 anywhere in them; (b) un-bumped, exactly one stamped compile before the new verb and 6/8GB as at BASE; (c) the new verb's --comment run=2 and its --cpu/--memory 4/6GB.

payload.body:
examiner (task 1): `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_own_proofs.mjs` is written and red at BASE for one reason — the implementation does not exist yet.

Red at BASE, assertion by assertion (soft-assert run, so every leg was reached rather than stopping at the first):

- leg (a) [M1] — `impl:T1` carries `TEST COMMAND: bash check.sh` (the run-wide suite, via `implTestCmdLine`/`namesProofTest`) and no `PROOFS:` block; same for `impl:T2` in the no-`Run:`/no-`Check:` scenario.
- leg (b) [M2] — `fix:T1:0` carries `TEST COMMAND: bash t1_test.sh` (the exam command, via `fixTestCmdLine`) and no block.
- leg (d) [M4] — all four engine symbols present, `TEST COMMAND` present in `implementer.md`, and neither role file names `PROOFS:`. Note `fix.md` does NOT contain the string `TEST COMMAND` at BASE, so that half of the grep is already zero — it says the same thing in its own words, and the exam's extra assertion that each role file NAMES `PROOFS:` is what keeps `fix.md` from passing by doing nothing.

Green at BASE, and meant to be — these are the preservation clauses:

- leg (c) [M3] — the examiner's one `TEST COMMAND:` line already names the exam command.
- leg (e) [M5] — the reconciler already carries the run-wide line and no block. The scenario is real, not vacuous: the sim's implementer writes the rig's `BROKEN` marker, the folded tree's `bash check.sh` goes red, and the precondition asserts `reconcile:wave1:1` was actually dispatched before reading its prompt (the stub then removes the marker and reports FIXED, so the wave still adopts).
- leg (f) [M6] — both survivor sims are present with their sentinel.

Whole file runs in about half a second; `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` is green with it in the sweep (15 sims, 0 offenders). Nothing returned unsatisfiable.

For the implementer: the exam reads LINES, not substrings — `testCmdLinesOf` filters lines that BEGIN `TEST COMMAND:`, because `implementer.md` line 7 and `reconcile.md` line 20 mention the phrase in prose at BASE and that is M4's grep to answer, not M1's. And the block's body is read as the lines under a line that is exactly `PROOFS:`, up to the next `KEY:` line or a blank line, so where the block sits among the other input lines is left free.

payload.author: impl:2@run-128
payload.body: task 2 done. The stamped compile now follows the run number: `launch` builds `compileFor(n)` and a `sizeFromCompile(payload)` helper, compiles once for the first N (so the billing-capacity refusal still fires before any mutation, on a size that is stamp-invariant), and hands `pushPlan` both `compiled: firstCompiled` and `recompile: compileFor`. `pushPlan` carries a `payload` alongside `n`, passes it to `kataStep(n, payload)`, recompiles after the purge on a bump, and returns the winning N's compile as `plan.compiled`; `launch` reads width/cpu/memory off that for the `new` verb. Verified against a throwaway bump sim (first push refused non-fast-forward, ls-remote then answering run-1 taken, the two stamps answering payloads of different widths): stamped compiles were run-1 then run-2, the surviving project was popmechanic-smoke-run-2 with run-1's purged, its sheets' landing paths named exams/run_2/, and the verb carried run=2 with --cpu/--memory computed from the second compile. `node fleet/tests/test_launch_size.mjs` and the full `python3 -m pytest -p no:xdist` (132 passed) are green. One disclosure for the reviewer: on a bump the first N's project IS still filed and then purged (BASE's order — the plan commit embeds kata.json, so the filing must precede the push), so a fake hub's recorded call list still contains one run_1 createIssue from the purged project; it is the surviving filing that carries run_2 everywhere.

payload.author: exam:2@run-128
payload.body:
Exam written at fleet/tests/test_launch_bump.mjs. Red at BASE on one assertion — leg (a)'s 'two stamped compiles, run-1 then run-2: got ["run-1"]' — with the bump itself already proven (result.run is 2, plan branch ultra/plan-run-2), so the failure reads as the absent recompile and nothing else. Verified green against a throwaway implementation (compileFor(n) handed to pushPlan, recompiled after the bump, the size and the hub filing re-read off the returned payload); that patch was reverted and the tree is BASE plus the exam. fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs sweeps the new file with 0 offenders.

Reading of one leg a later session should not have to reconstruct: leg (b)'s clause 'the narrowed sizing sim still prints its sentinel' is NOT a spawn in this exam. fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs M4 forbids any test_*.mjs from spawning another test_*.mjs, and its leg (e) forbids even naming one to existsSync/statSync/accessSync — an exam that ran test_launch_size.mjs would turn that probe red. The Proof's second Run: (node fleet/tests/test_launch_size.mjs | grep -q 'ALL TESTS PASSED') is what executes it, and the driver runs that itself. What this exam does instead is read test_launch_size.mjs's source and pin that its leg (c) marker and its sentinel line survive — the narrowing is in place, not a deletion. Everything else in legs (a), (b) and (c) is driven live.

Second reading worth keeping: M3's 'the size the new verb carries is computed from the recompiled payload' is unfalsifiable if both compiles answer the same waves, since (as the task's Context says) the widest wave is the same for every stamp in the real compiler. So the compiler stub answers per --stamp — run-1 gives waves 2/10/1 (--cpu 6 --memory 8GB under the 6/8GB caps) and run-2 gives 2/4/1 (--cpu 4 --memory 6GB). An implementation that sizes off the payload it no longer files is red on leg (c). A stamp the stub was not prepared for exits non-zero, so a third compile is a refusal rather than a silent JSON parse failure.
